key_insight: Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI) directly visualizes internal charge-carrier motion in operating semiconductor devices by mapping local electric-field changes in real space and time.
engineering_relevance: This gives solar-cell and detector engineers a non-invasive way to connect microscopic transport processes to measurable current, helping diagnose losses, trapping, and transport bottlenecks in real devices.
method: Pockels-based imaging of local electric-field variations
Real-space, time-resolved tracking of photogenerated carrier clouds
Correlation of internal carrier evolution with conduction and displacement currents
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstration in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution, showing direct observation of carrier dynamics and morphology evolution.
watch_item: Broad adoption depends on the device having a sufficiently strong electro-optic response, so materials or stacks with weak Pockels sensitivity may be harder to image reliably.
paper_title: Direct Spatiotemporal Imaging of Charge Carrier Dynamics in Operative Semiconductor Devices
